Why · How · What A long chat blurs in the middle, for a different reason than a long phone call: what fills the window, and how to see it. Why The AI forgets what you told it an hour ago. Think of a long phone call: you remember how it began, how it ended and one odd moment, and the middle blurs. ( ) A long chat blurs the same way. How Attention thins out as the window fills. Every message goes in again, and the first lines and the newest messages draw the most attention; the middle and the rest fade. ( ) What Far more than your chat sits in the window. Saved memory loads at the start, a web search drops whole pages in, and near the limit the app may summarise old messages. ( ) Try every part and control above.

About People forget the middle too In free recall of a word list, the first and the last items are remembered best and the middle worst, and an item that stands out is remembered better than its neighbours 1 2 . This is lab evidence from word lists, so applying it to a long call or chat is an inference (research COG-0001). Sources (2) Murdock, The serial position effect of free recall ( opens in a new tab ) doi.org Glanzer and Cunitz, Two storage mechanisms in free recall ( opens in a new tab ) doi.org Position and length both matter Models use information best at the start and end of the input and worst in the middle, and the first tokens draw strong attention even when they mean nothing 1 2 . Quality also falls as the window fills, even with perfect retrieval 3 4 . The strength differs per model, and the mechanism is the authors' account, not proof for every product (research LLM-0006, LLM-0007). Sources (4) Liu et al., Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts ( opens in a new tab ) arxiv.org Xiao et al., Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks ( opens in a new tab ) arxiv.org Hsieh et al., RULER: What's the Real Context Size of Your Long-Context Language Models? ( opens in a new tab ) arxiv.org Du et al., Context Length Alone Hurts LLM Performance Despite Perfect Retrieval ( opens in a new tab ) arxiv.org What else fills the window Claude Code loads its memory at the start of every conversation, as context that counts against the window 1 . A search tool returns page content that sits in the window as input tokens 2 . Near the limit the Claude app summarises earlier messages; for other apps no vendor documents it 3 (research LLM-0008, LLM-0009, LLM-0010). Sources (3) Anthropic, How Claude remembers your project ( opens in a new tab ) code.claude.com Anthropic, Web search tool (Claude API documentation) ( opens in a new tab ) platform.claude.com Anthropic, Compaction overview ( opens in a new tab ) platform.claude.com
